Issued at 353 AM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

SW flow aloft across the central US, feeding plume of very hot air 
(850mb temps up into the 25C range) and steep mid-level lapse rates 
from the SW US across the central and northern Plains attm. Broad 
troughing over the W US, including an upper low and attendant 100kt 
upper jet poking into the PacNW...and a PV max swirling almost due 
north through MT into Alberta. Broad troughing over eastern Canada 
with influences across the Lower Great Lakes and New England where 
the bulk of the convection has been ongoing as of 4z. Confluence and 
zonal flow over the Great Lakes between upper ridge over the SE and 
upper low near James Bay; a plume of deeper moisture (pwats at or 
above 1.5in) stretches along this confluence zone from the Plains 
eastward through the Upper MS Valley and into the Lower Great Lakes. 
Now that remnants of "Edouard" are tracking deeper into TX, 
starting to see better Gulf moisture transport north up the MS 
Valley. SW LLJ is a bit stronger tonight across the Plains as 
well...upwards of 40kts or better at 850mb, more or less 
orthogonal to aforementioned boundary from the Plains to Lower 
MI...but does turn to the SE across the Northern Plains up into 
Canada ahead of the occluded surface low in Alberta ahead of 
aforementioned PV maximum. Low-level col region and/or 
deformation axis over the Upper Midwest attm between upstream 
feature and last lobes of energy swirling around through Ontario
on the backside of the James Bay area upper low. Slightly 
cooler and slightly less humid air around attm, with Tds across 
most of northern Lower in the upper 50s to lower 60s, vs the 
juicy upper 60s to lower 70s we had the day before...though that
juicy air mass remains across S. MI south of aforementioned 
boundary. 

PV over MT and a little wind of PV ahead of it track northward 
toward Canada today...resulting in the baroclinic zone buckling 
northward as upper low over James Bay slowly releases its grip on 
our weather...and will anticipate an increased threat for 
showers/storms tonight into Friday morning along said boundary, 
including into northern MI. Will need to keep an eye out for 
convection to ride the ridge axis into the Great Lakes Friday night 
into Saturday, which could lead to a damper start to the holiday 
weekend. It also appears high pressure will attempt to ooze back 
into northern MI from Ontario this weekend as the ridge axis 
strengthens just upstream; this will put a confluence zone likely 
well to our north across Canada, and may need to keep an eye out for 
any of this activity to try to drift down the thickness gradient 
into the Great Lakes. Signals point toward the ridge axis building 
into the Upper Midwest and even Great Lakes for Labor Day and 
perhaps beyond...with strengthening easterly flow across southern 
Canada and perhaps parts of the Upper Midwest...as energy ejects out 
of the western trough and drives pressure falls across the northern
Plains. The overall pattern going into midweek next week suggests we 
will remain in a warm, moist, and potentially unsettled environment 
(barring any mid-level stability provided by the ridge)...though the 
evolution of the ejecting energy is unclear and will determine how 
strong a surface response is had in the Great Lakes next week. 
Increasing uncertainty in the pattern beyond the middle of next 
week, primarily in the evolution/strength/position of upstream 
troughing, which will impact how much of an influence the ridge axis 
will continue to exert on our area going into the second weekend of 
September. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances today/tonight... Current expectation is for 
upstream convection (currently struggling to develop over IA as of 
6z but finally taking shape around 7z over N. IA/S. MN) to 
eventually develop across MN/WI this morning as the deformation axis 
lifts northeastward. If this early morning batch does not hold 
together well, it may take till 12-15z to get going, which is when 
there is better synoptic-level support for ascent. Either way, 
will look for upstream convection to track generally eastward into 
Lower MI with time through the day. Think the greatest instability 
will remain to our south and west...but we will be on the 
instability gradient as a plume of steeper lapse rates aloft sneaks 
in this morning and the boundary (and juicier boundary layer) lifts 
back northward. Sticky wicket for spicier storms is mid-level 
warmth, as it would put something of a cap on deep moist convection 
potential this afternoon, particularly if we do not moisten/warm 
enough in the low levels to overcome this cap (and this may be 
harder to do as we may end up on the north and likely, stratiform-
rain-with-embedded-thunder side of the boundary). Jet max moving
